title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
summary: DARIC replaces full prefix prefill (and prior recomputation-based cache-reuse methods such as CacheBlend-style approaches) for repeated long contexts by storing position-independent KV caches and recomputing only a subset of tokens selected by empirical KV-deviation distributions, with a lightweight architecture intended to integrate with standard inference engines like vLLM. Costs include storing and managing reusable KV caches per document chunk, added integration and token-selection logic in the serving stack, and a residual recomputation pass whose overhead depends on the selected token fraction. It can fail when prefix reuse patterns are rare (unique or non-overlapping queries yield no benefit), when the assumed deviation distribution does not hold for a given model or tokenizer, or when third-party APIs are used, since the method requires access to KV-cache internals unavailable through black-box endpoints.
rationale: The claimed TTFT speedup is directly relevant to constrained-infrastructure RAG and agentic serving on a single GPU, but the gain is workload-dependent and requires engine-level integration plus validation against existing prefix-caching features, so small-scale testing is warranted before adoption.
technique: Distribution-aware KV cache reuse for long contexts
